statements.text: I live in a tiny apartment in Tennoji, about ten minutes' walk from the station.
I'm a nurse on the pediatric ward at Naniwa General, three night shifts a week.
My cat Mochi is a three-year-old rescue and he absolutely hates the vacuum cleaner.
Midosuji line to work every morning, and it's a sardine can.
My sister Mio bakes at a little boulangerie in Kobe and keeps sending me melon pan.
Started Korean on Duolingo, fifteen minutes a day, purely because of K-dramas.
Still limping along on my iPhone 12, the battery is dead by lunch.
Hikaru Utada is basically the only thing on my train playlist right now.
Kenta surprised me with a Pixel 9 for my birthday, no more battery panic!
Joined a Saturday morning yoga class near Shinsaibashi.
I've gone vegetarian since the new year, it's easier in Osaka than I expected.
Transferred to the ICU at Naniwa General this week, my feet are destroyed.
Mochi has a little brother now, a tabby kitten called Kinako.
Turns out I'm allergic to shellfish, found out the hard way over a bowl of ramen in Hakata.
Kenta's an engineer at Panasonic, so he gets a weird no-overtime Wednesday every week.
Kenta and I signed for a 2LDK in Fukushima ward, moving in this weekend.
I bike to the hospital now, fifteen minutes door to door, and I've stopped dreading mornings.
Mio left the boulangerie and now works at a specialty coffee roaster in Kyoto.
Running the Yodogawa riverside path every Sunday, trying to be ready for a 10k this November.
Swapped Duolingo for a weekly Korean class in Umeda, I need an actual human correcting me.
Kenta's mum is allergic to cats, so she turns up with antihistamines every time she visits.
Dropped the Pixel in the bath and killed it, so I'm on a spare Galaxy A55 from Kenta for now.
Fish is back on the menu, vegetarian didn't survive night shifts, so basically pescatarian now.
Also picked up Spanish on Tandem, chatting with a guy from Valencia on Thursdays.
Registered for the Himeji Castle 10k on November 8th.
Fujii Kaze has taken over my playlists, Utada has been benched.
Mochi had his teeth cleaned at the vet today and sulked for hours.

statements.text: Teaching physics and maths at Tertnes high school, this is my 26th year in the classroom.
Still driving the 2014 Volvo V70 diesel, 240,000 km on the clock and it refuses to die.
The doctor put me on amlodipine for my blood pressure, 5 mg every morning.
Odin, our Labrador, is nine now and slower on the hills.
Ingrid works as a nurse at Haukeland, mostly day shifts these days.
Black filter coffee, four cups a day, I know, I know.
I'm building a clinker dinghy in the garage, been at it every Sunday since spring.
Our house is in Fana, about twenty-five minutes south of the city centre.
Ribbe and aquavit on Christmas Eve like every year, asleep on the sofa by eight.
I take the Bybanen light rail to school most days, gives me time to mark papers.
Started Italian on Babbel, want to be semi-conversational before our trip to Puglia.
Doctor says cut the coffee, so it's two cups a day now and green tea in the afternoon.
My knee gave out on the hike up Ulriken, the MRI says torn meniscus.
Sofie is expecting, due in July!
Our principal is Kari Sunde, and she wants me to coach the physics olympiad team.
Odin's a yellow Lab, by the way, with a very grey muzzle these days.
Finally had the arthroscopy on my knee, two weeks on crutches and bored out of my mind.
Mats got a job as an engineer at Equinor in Stavanger.
The Model Y arrived on Friday, the V70 is gone, and I keep reaching for a clutch that isn't there.
Also started restoring Ingrid's grandfather's rocking chair, sanding is a nightmare.
Swapped amlodipine for ramipril, the swollen ankles were a pain.
Last day before the summer break was Friday, I'm off until mid-August.
Sofie had a baby girl on Monday, Linnea, seven pounds something.
Launched the dinghy at Os this morning, named her Snorre, and she floats!
Got an e-bike and now cycle to work, forty minutes each way.
Kari Sunde retired and Terje Moe is our new principal, started this week.
Ingrid has started French lessons on Wednesday evenings, she's keen.
Cut coffee out completely, decaf and herbal tea only after the blood pressure scare.

statements.text: I've lived in this adobe house on Candelaria since 1989 and I'm not going anywhere.
My flip phone does everything I need, so don't try to sell me a smartphone.
Pepito the parakeet chirps all day long, so I keep the radio on for him.
I take metformin twice a day for my sugar, and the pharmacist set up a little weekly pill box for me.
Dr. Patel at Lovelace is my doctor, he's looked after me for eleven years.
I sing alto in the choir at St. Charles, rehearsal is Wednesday nights.
My daughter Lucia in Phoenix is a dental hygienist and lectures me about flossing.
Marcus's two kids, Mateo and Camila, are driving down from Denver to stay for Christmas.
Still driving my 2009 Buick Lucerne, only 61,000 miles on it.
Cafe con leche every morning, two sugars, and don't you judge me.
Cataract surgery on my left eye is booked for February 3rd.
Joined a bridge club that meets Thursday afternoons at the community center.
The cataract surgery went wonderfully, my left eye can see the blue of the Sandias again.
A neighbor couldn't keep her blue budgie Chula, so now she's mine.
Dr. Patel retired last month, so now I see Dr. Okafor at the UNM clinic.
Lucia talked me into an iPhone SE, I'm learning how to FaceTime the grandkids.
Tomatoes and green chile are in the ground, the garden is back in business.
My daughter-in-law Elena is a pharmacist at Kaiser and sends me photos every Sunday.
Dr. Okafor added Jardiance on top of the metformin, one pill each morning, because my A1C was too high.
Sold the Candelaria house and moved into a one-bedroom at Sandia Vista, east side.
Sold the Buick to the neighbor's grandson, Sandia Vista has a shuttle and I don't miss driving.
Had lunch with Rosa at Garduno's yesterday, the sopapillas were enormous.
Only a pot of basil on the balcony now, the tomato days are over.
Got Phonak hearing aids from the audiologist, I can hear the choir again.
Pepito passed away in his sleep this week, eleven years old, and I cried more than I expected.
Switched to decaf cafe con leche, my pressure's been creeping up.
Dr. Okafor left the UNM clinic so I'm seeing Brenda Wells, a nurse practitioner, at the Sandia Vista clinic.

statements.text: I'm a structural engineer at Brightwater Builders, mostly high-rise work around Lekki.
We rent a three-bedroom flat in Yaba, and the landlord keeps promising to fix the water pump.
My ride is a 2011 Toyota Camry, Tokunbo, and the AC is the only thing that complains.
Getting to site takes about ninety minutes each way, Third Mainland Bridge is my sworn enemy.
Ngozi, my wife, is a pharmacist at a hospital in Ikeja.
Our landlord sold the building, so we've moved into a flat in Surulere and the boxes are still everywhere.
Five-a-side football every Saturday morning, my knees hate me but the banter is worth it.
The generator in our compound runs on petrol and the fuel bill is killing me.
Ngozi and I are expecting our first baby in March!
My phone is a Tecno Camon 30 and honestly the camera is decent.
Spent Christmas in Enugu with my parents, my mum's jollof is no match for Lagos jollof but don't tell her.
Trying intermittent fasting, sixteen hours off, nothing to eat after 7pm.
Booked my PMP exam for 14 May and I'm studying every night after dinner.
Solar panels and an inverter went in last week, and I sold the generator to my cousin.
Chidi arrived on the 4th, 3.4 kg and already has Ngozi's frown.
Chidi's first-month photos are all on my new-to-me iPhone 14, the Tecno lives in a drawer now.
Resigned from Brightwater, I start at Arcadia Infrastructure on Monday as a senior structural engineer.
Doing French on Busuu for twenty minutes before bed, in case Arcadia ever sends me to Abidjan.
I passed the PMP!! Four months of misery paid off.
The new office is on Victoria Island, so I leave at 5:30am now and I'm there in about an hour.
Dropped the fasting experiment, with a newborn at home sleeping beats an eating window.
The Ikoyi tower package is due to the client at the end of September.
My manager at Arcadia is Folake Bankole, she keeps meetings short, which I love.
My younger brother Obinna is a junior doctor in Manchester.
Ajah estate package deadline is mid-December, so that one can wait.
The Camry finally went to the scrapyard and I picked up a 2016 Honda CR-V from a dealer in Lekki.
Ngozi's boss at the hospital is Dr. Adeyemi, a very serious man.
Arcadia just made me principal structural engineer, three months in and I'm still processing it.

statements.text: Final year of my architecture degree at RMIT and studio is eating my entire life.
I'm in a share terrace in Brunswick East with three housemates, one of whom steals my yoghurt.
Weekends I work at a bike shop on Sydney Road, mostly fixing punctures and drinking bad coffee.
I tram into uni, the 96 when it actually shows up.
My Pixel 7's screen is a spiderweb but it still works, so no upgrade yet.
Turns out I'm lactose intolerant, which explains four years of stomach aches, so it's oat flat whites from now on.
I'm still on my 2019 MacBook Pro and the fan sounds like a jet engine.
Been vegetarian since my birthday in October, mum is coping.
Fine Spotify, yes, I did listen to Phoebe Bridgers for nine hundred minutes last year.
Splurged on a MacBook Air M3 with my bike-shop savings, the jet engine has retired.
Started bouldering at Northside on Tuesday nights, my forearms are not impressed.
Learning Japanese on WaniKani, ten minutes every morning before my coffee.
My brother Jonas is a FIFO electrician in the Pilbara, two weeks on and one off.
Signed a lease on my own one-bedroom in Northcote, finally some quiet.
It's the bike for me now, thirty minutes along the Merri Creek trail to the city.
Back from ten days in Kyoto, and my Japanese survived a ramen vending machine.
The bike is an olive-green Surly Cross-Check, in case anyone asks.
Quit the bike shop, I'm interning three days a week at a small studio called Fenwick+Lowe in Collingwood.
My thesis is on adaptive reuse of old Brunswick warehouses.
Going vegan for June and quite possibly forever, my nan is horrified.
Signed up for Auslan classes on Thursday nights, because sign language has always fascinated me.
Vegan month is over and I caved, back to vegetarian because cheese won.
Day three on my new iPhone 15 and I already miss the Pixel's camera.
Deleted Spotify and moved my playlists to Apple Music since I'm on the iPhone now.
My supervisor made me ditch the warehouses, so the thesis is now a timber community library.
Thesis submission is the 30th of October and I've got about eleven pages.
Fenwick+Lowe's competition entry is due on the 14th of October, so it's late nights all round.
